        - generic
          - heading "1. Model Introduction" [level=2, ref=e91]
          - link "Permalink: 1. Model Introduction" [ref=e92]
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Kimi K2 is a state-of-the-art mixture-of-experts (MoE) language model with 32 billion activated parameters and 1 trillion total parameters. Trained with the Muon optimizer, Kimi K2 achieves exceptional performance across frontier knowledge, reasoning, and coding tasks while being meticulously optimized for agentic capabilities."
        - generic
          - heading "Key Features" [level=3, ref=e93]
          - link "Permalink: Key Features" [ref=e94]
        - list
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "• "
            - StaticText "Large-Scale Training: Pre-trained a 1T parameter MoE model on 15.5T tokens with zero training instability."
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "• "
            - StaticText "MuonClip Optimizer: We apply the Muon optimizer to an unprecedented scale, and develop novel optimization techniques to resolve instabilities while scaling up."
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "• "
            - StaticText "Agentic Intelligence: Specifically designed for tool use, reasoning, and autonomous problem-solving."
        - generic
          - heading "Model Variants" [level=3, ref=e95]
          - link "Permalink: Model Variants" [ref=e96]
        - list
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "• "
            - strong
            - StaticText ": The foundation model, a strong start for researchers and builders who want full control for fine-tuning and custom solutions."
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "• "
            - strong
            - StaticText ": The post-trained model, best for drop-in, general-purpose chat and agentic experiences. It is a reflex-grade model without long thinking."

        - superscript
          - StaticText "• Bold denotes global SOTA, and underlined denotes open-source SOTA."
        - LineBreak "\n"
        - superscript
          - StaticText "• Data points marked with * are directly from the model's tech report or blog."
        - LineBreak "\n"
        - superscript
          - StaticText "• All metrics, except for SWE-bench Verified (Agentless), are evaluated with an 8k output token length. SWE-bench Verified (Agentless) is limited to a 16k output token length."
        - LineBreak "\n"
        - superscript
          - StaticText "• Kimi K2 achieves 65.8% pass@1 on the SWE-bench Verified tests with bash/editor tools (single-attempt patches, no test-time compute). It also achieves a 47.3% pass@1 on the SWE-bench Multilingual tests under the same conditions. Additionally, we report results on SWE-bench Verified tests (71.6%) that leverage parallel test-time compute by sampling multiple sequences and selecting the single best via an internal scoring model."
        - LineBreak "\n"
        - superscript
          - StaticText "• To ensure the stability of the evaluation, we employed avg@k on the AIME, HMMT, CNMO, PolyMath-en, GPQA-Diamond, EvalPlus, Tau2."
        - LineBreak "\n"
        - superscript
          - StaticText "• Some data points have been omitted due to prohibitively expensive evaluation costs."

          - heading "4. Deployment" [level=2, ref=e105]
          - link "Permalink: 4. Deployment" [ref=e106]
        - StaticText "Note"
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "You can access Kimi K2's API on "
          - link "https://platform.moonshot.ai" [ref=e107]
          - StaticText " , we provide an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API for you."
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "The Anthropic-compatible API maps temperature by "
          - code
            - StaticText "real_temperature = request_temperature * 0.6"
          - StaticText " for better compatiblity with existing applications."
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Our model checkpoints are stored in block-fp8 format, you can find it on "
          - link "Huggingface" [ref=e108]
          - StaticText "."
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Currently, it is recommended to run Kimi-K2 on the following inference engines:"
        - list

            - ListMarker "• "
            - StaticText "TensorRT-LLM"

        - generic
          - heading "5. Model Usage" [level=2, ref=e110]
          - link "Permalink: 5. Model Usage" [ref=e111]
        - generic
          - heading "Chat Completion" [level=3, ref=e112]
          - link "Permalink: Chat Completion" [ref=e113]
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Once the local inference service is set up, you can interact with it through the chat endpoint:"
        - generic
          - generic
            - StaticText "def simple_chat(client: OpenAI, model_name: str):\n    messages = [\n        {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": \"You are Kimi, an AI assistant created by Moonshot AI.\"},\n        {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Please give a brief self-introduction.\"}]},\n    ]\n    response = client.chat.completions.create(\n        model=model_name,\n        messages=messages,\n        stream=False,\n        temperature=0.6,\n        max_tokens=256\n    )\n    print(response.choices[0].message.content)"
          - button "Copy code to clipboard" [ref=e114]
        - StaticText "Note"
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "The recommended temperature for Kimi-K2-Instruct is "
          - code
            - StaticText "temperature = 0.6"
          - StaticText ". If no special instructions are required, the system prompt is a good default."
        - separator
        - generic
          - heading "Tool Calling" [level=3, ref=e115]
          - link "Permalink: Tool Calling" [ref=e116]
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Kimi-K2-Instruct has strong tool-calling capabilities. To enable them, you need to pass the list of available tools in each request, then the model will autonomously decide when and how to invoke them."
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "The following example demonstrates calling a weather tool end-to-end:"
        - generic
          - generic
            - StaticText "# Your tool implementation\ndef get_weather(city: str) -> dict:\n    return {\"weather\": \"Sunny\"}\n\n# Tool schema definition\ntools = [{\n    \"type\": \"function\",\n    \"function\": {\n        \"name\": \"get_weather\",\n        \"description\": \"Retrieve current weather information. Call this when the user asks about the weather.\",\n        \"parameters\": {\n            \"type\": \"object\",\n            \"required\": [\"city\"],\n            \"properties\": {\n                \"city\": {\n                    \"type\": \"string\",\n                    \"description\": \"Name of the city\"\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}]\n\n# Map tool names to their implementations\ntool_map = {\n    \"get_weather\": get_weather\n}\n\ndef tool_call_with_client(client: OpenAI, model_name: str):\n    messages = [\n        {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": \"You are Kimi, an AI assistant created by Moonshot AI.\"},\n        {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"What's the weather like in Beijing today? Use the tool to check.\"}\n    ]\n    finish_reason = None\n    while finish_reason is None or finish_reason == \"tool_calls\":\n        completion = client.chat.completions.create(\n            model=model_name,\n            messages=messages,\n            temperature=0.6,\n            tools=tools,          # tool list defined above\n            tool_choice=\"auto\"\n        )\n        choice = completion.choices[0]\n        finish_reason = choice.finish_reason\n        if finish_reason == \"tool_calls\":\n            messages.append(choice.message)\n            for tool_call in choice.message.tool_calls:\n                tool_call_name = tool_call.function.name\n                tool_call_arguments = json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments)\n                tool_function = tool_map[tool_call_name]\n                tool_result = tool_function(**tool_call_arguments)\n                print(\"tool_result:\", tool_result)\n\n                messages.append({\n                    \"role\": \"tool\",\n                    \"tool_call_id\": tool_call.id,\n                    \"name\": tool_call_name,\n                    \"content\": json.dumps(tool_result)\n                })\n    print(\"-\" * 100)\n    print(choice.message.content)"
          - button "Copy code to clipboard" [ref=e117]
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "The "
          - code
            - StaticText "tool_call_with_client"
          - StaticText " function implements the pipeline from user query to tool execution. This pipeline requires the inference engine to support Kimi-K2’s native tool-parsing logic. For streaming output and manual tool-parsing, see the "
          - link "Tool Calling Guide" [ref=e118]
          - StaticText "."
        - separator
